## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish forewings with darker patches, fine crosslines, and a bark-like pattern that helps it blend into tree trunks, dead leaves, and dry vegetation. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where suitable host plants and sheltered resting sites occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on plant material and serve as part of the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
